absent: Behavior of host invalidation start handling and generic host address range dispatch beyond the completion path shown.
Architecture specific dirty synchronization and re arming and attribute and virtualization callbacks.
Full layouts of VM and slot and cache and range structures beyond fields observed in use.
Global VM list lifetime and locking beyond publication and preempt notification effects.
Exact numeric values of error codes and flag bits and slot limits and ioctl numbers.
Coalesced input setup and irq routing and eventfd and bus dispatch behavior.
Memory attribute support mask and architecture post set effects.

findings.text: A helper revoking cached host mappings overlapping a supplied host interval exists in two builds, an inert inline performing no action and an active routine scanning registered caches and withdrawing usability from overlapping entries.

Traversal of registered address caches holds a VM wide spin guard across the walk while each entry is first examined under shared interrupt disabling access and only apparently affected entries are re examined under exclusive interrupt disabling access before usability is withdrawn.

An address cache entry counts as overlapping when its usability marking is set and its page reference is not an error placeholder for a missing slot and its host address lies at or after the interval start and strictly before the interval end, with entry length ignored because each entry covers a single page.

Completion of a host memory invalidation interval forwards the interval to VM address handling with blocking posture inherited from the host notification and then participates in a paired active depth count that wakes a waiter when the last concurrent invalidation finishes.

Active host invalidation depth is guarded by a dedicated spin guard and decremented on interval completion with an expectation that depth was nonzero, with a wake issued only on transition to zero under the premise that at most one waiter sleeps under the slot mutex.

Host aging queries share tracing and range aging delegation across three callbacks, where the flushing variant may request translation flushing subject to build time elision control while the non flushing clearing variant and the single address test variant never request flushing.

A constant operations table for host memory notifications provides members for interval start, interval end, flushing clear, non flushing clear, test and release, and VM initialization attaches this table to the VM notifier before registering against the current process address space.
Release of the host address space association triggers a full shadow state flush performed inside a sleepable read critical section indexed against the VM.
The power management callback of a VM resolves its owning VM from the notifier record and delegates the event to an architecture specific handler, propagating the architecture result unchanged.

Power notification setup has two builds, one assigning maximal ordering priority so VM suspension precedes other subsystems and registering the callback, and another providing an inert initializer performing neither assignment nor registration.

VM debug visibility uses a directory named from the creating process identifier combined with the supplied file name, duplicate names are reported at throttled warning level and treated as success without replacement, and directory establishment failure is treated as non fatal absence.
Existence check and directory creation for VM debug state are serialized by a function local static mutex held only across lookup and creation, not across later file population.

Per VM debug statistics storage reserves one slot per VM wide descriptor plus one slot per vCPU descriptor, where each populated slot records its owning VM and its descriptor reference and whether it aggregates VM wide or vCPU accumulated counters.

Generic debug file population is followed by an architecture hook, and any allocation exhaustion during population discards partially created state through a common destroy path and reports resource exhaustion.
Architecture specific VM debug extension defaults to an inert weakly linked routine that architectures may override to add further entries.

Each address space maintains two slot sets whose generation is seeded from the address space index so generations differ across spaces, with cached tree roots and identifier hash and node marker and last used hint prepared before the first set is published through an RCU assignment.

A new VM prepares distinct mutexes for general control and interrupt control and slot mutation including an architecture slot mutex, plus spin guards for host invalidation and address cache lists, alongside sleepable read structures and resizable collections for vCPUs and buses.

VM construction moves from architecture allocation through host memory capture and generic subsystem setup and slot and bus preparation into architecture initialization and virtualization enablement and notification setup and debug setup and global list publication, with any failure unwinding only already acquired resources in reverse order.

Before debug setup the VM debug handle is poisoned to a not found marker so dependent file creations fail safely when no directory exists, and a compile time assertion constrains the configured slot count to a signed short range.
MMU lock initialization is build dependent, with one configuration preparing a reader writer primitive and another preparing an exclusive spin primitive for the same VM field.

A reference release variant drops the VM user count without destroying the object and warns when the drop released the final reference, so callers retain at least one remaining reference across the call.
Closure of the VM file handle releases associated interrupt file descriptors and then releases the VM reference, always reporting success.

Bulk acquisition of all vCPU mutexes requires the VM mutex already held and reports busy when creation is in progress, otherwise it attempts nesting aware acquisition of each vCPU guard and on first contention releases those already taken and reports interruption.
The first generation memory region flag set is defined as the combination of the dirty page logging request and the read only request.
The memory region establishment request rejects slot numbers outside the user visible range and otherwise serializes against concurrent slot mutation while delegating to the generic region installer.
User requests installing regions or retrieving or clearing dirty state are serialized by the VM slot mutex held across the whole inner operation.

Dirty tracking requests encode address space in the high half and slot identifier in the low half of a combined value, with requests outside the architecture address space count or user slot limit rejected as invalid and requests for absent slots or slots lacking a bitmap rejected as missing.
Bitmap based dirty queries are unavailable when the VM uses an alternative dirty ring mechanism, in which case the operations fail with a distinct exclusivity error rather than consulting any bitmap.

Non protective dirty query synchronizes architecture dirty state into the slot bitmap, determines whether any word is nonzero, transfers the bitmap to user memory with fault reported on copy failure, and signals dirtiness and the located slot through separate out parameters.

Protective dirty query offers a manual mode sharing the live bitmap without flushing and an automatic mode atomically harvesting set words into a secondary buffer under MMU guard while re enabling hardware tracking for harvested ranges, flushing remote translations only when harvesting occurred.

Harvesting and re arming of dirty bits during protective query and during selective clearing occurs with the VM MMU guard held, with remote translation flush performed after release when any bit was collected or cleared.
The user request for retrieving dirty state wraps the protective query worker with slot mutex protection and propagates its status.

Selective dirty clearing requires a sixty four page aligned start and a range fully contained in the slot extent and a length either sixty four page aligned or extending exactly to the slot end, otherwise the request is rejected as invalid.

Selective clearing synchronizes architecture state and stages a user supplied mask, then under MMU guard atomically clears only mask bits actually set and re enables hardware tracking solely for bits truly cleared, flushing remote translations only when at least one bit transitioned.
The user request for clearing dirty state wraps the selective clearing worker with slot mutex protection and propagates its status.

Guest frame interval handling walks every address space and each slot overlapping the interval with interval ends clamped to slot bounds and empty intersections skipped, acquiring the MMU guard lazily on first overlap and invoking an optional lock hook once before per slot handler calls whose combined outcome may trigger a global translation flush.

The guest frame walk holds no MMU guard when no slot overlaps, otherwise holds it from the first overlap through all handler invocations, with an optional global flush issued before release when requested and when any handler reported effect.

Preparation for attribute change unconditionally records the affected guest frame interval in the invalidation set regardless of whether translation removal proves necessary, then delegates to the architecture preparation callback and propagates its boolean outcome.

The memory attribute request rejects nonzero flags and unsupported attribute bits and empty or wrapping ranges and unaligned address or size, then converts the byte interval to guest frame numbers and delegates to the range installer.

Absent attributes are stored as a null value while present attributes are encoded as small integer values in the VM attribute array, with a compile time check that the user attribute width matches the native word width so generic attributes assume a wide word environment.

Attribute installation exits early when the whole interval already carries the wanted value, otherwise it pre reserves backing for every frame when setting nonzero values and brackets the stores with pre and post guest frame walks respectively opening and closing MMU invalidation, holding the slot mutex throughout while yielding periodically during long loops.
A helper reports whether a guest frame is currently exposed to the guest by resolving its slot and applying the slot visibility predicate.

A helper estimates host mapping granularity for a guest frame by translating to a host address and inspecting the covering virtual area under read protection, returning the area kernel page size on success and the base page size when translation fails or no area covers the address.

Transfers of dirty bitmaps between kernel and user memory treat access faults as distinct failures, and missing resources manifest as invalid or missing or exclusivity errors depending on cause without implying hardware state corruption.

Debug directory races yielding duplicates are contained by returning success after a throttled notice and releasing the extra reference, while allocation exhaustion during file creation triggers teardown of the partially built directory to avoid leaking handles.
